CT - Abdomen & Pelvis.title: CECT ABDOMEN
CT - Abdomen & Pelvis.content:
CECT ABDOMEN
The patient is a known case of chronic calcific pancreatitis with the dilated intra and extrahepatic biliary
radicles, splenomegaly, omental infarcts and bilateral renal calculus. Study compared with the previous CT
done on 22/02/2012.
There is dilatation of the entire jejunal loop with maximum luminal diameter of 3.8 cm. The transition zone is
at the level of the distal jejunum. There is a twist in the bowel loop at the level of transition zone. No
obvious stricture/mass lesion/extrinsic compression is noted.
The dilated bowel loops show normal wall enhancement. No pneumoperitoneum/pneumatosis intestinalis.
The distal small bowel loop is completely collapsed.
Minimal inter bowel free fluid is noted.
Minimal right pleural effusion is noted.
No other significant interval change is noted compared to the previous CT done on 22/02/2012.
IMPRESSION:
The patient is a known case of chronic calcific pancreatitis with the dilated intra and extra hepatic biliary
radicles, splenomegaly, omental infarcts and bilateral renal calculus. Study compared with the previous CT
done on 22/02/2012. Present study shows,
Imaging features are consistent with small bowel obstruction with transition zone at the level of distal
jejunum probably secondary to adhesions.
No features of the mesentric ischaemia/pneumoperitoneum/ pneumatosis intestinalis.

Clinical Details: Mass abdomen.
Serial sections of the abdomen were studied with oral and I.V.Bolus contrast.
The study shows normal anatomical configuration of the liver with uniform density. No focal or diffuse
pathology is noted.
The intrahepatic biliary radicles, portal and hepatic veins are normal.
The head, body and tail of the pancreas are well demonstrated and are normal in size, shape and attenuation.
Multiple lobulated conglomerate nodal homogenously enhancing mass measuring about 7.2 x 8.2 x 12.2cm (AP x TR x
CC) is noted in the retroperitoneum. Few nodes show necrosis and shows peripheral enhancement. No evidence of
calcification.
Anteriorly the lesion is seen extending upto the posterior wall of stomach. Posteriorly the lesion is reaching
upto the anterior margin of vertebra. Inferiorly the lesion is extending upto the level of aortic bifurcation.
Craniocaudally the lesion is extending from the level of Superior end plate of L1 to L5 level.
Loss of fat plane with left lateral wall of duodenum and posterior border of pancreas. Fat plane with bilateral
psoas muscles is lost possibly invasion.
The lesion is seen encasing the aorta and its branches. Caliber of the vessels is maintained. Aorta is
displaced anteriorly. No evidence of compression/ thrombosis. Inferior vena cava and bilateral renal veins are
deformed and displaced anteriorly. There is lateral deviation of bilateral ureters noted with mild
hydronephrosis of left kidney. The caliber of ureter is normal on both sides. Small bowel loops are displaced
anterolaterally.
The gall bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall.
No evidence of any stone, sludge or mass.
The spleen is normal with regard to size, position and morphology and displays uniform enhancement pattern.
Both the kidneys are normal in size, shape and position and show good excretion of contrast with adequate
demonstration of pelvicaliceal system.
The perinephric area is normal. Minimal thickening of bilateral anterior renal fascia noted.
The adrenals are normal on both sides.
The bowel loops are normal.
Minimal free fluid seen in the pelvis.
The bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall. No evidence of stone or mass.
Uterus and ovaries are normal.
Visualized bones are normal.
Visualized lung fields show no significant abnormality.
IMPRESSION:
Enlarged mesenteric and retroperitoneal adenopathy as detailed. Imaging findings are consistent with lymphoma.
Dr.V.Rajesh

CT - Abdomen & Pelvis.title: C.T. SCAN OF ABDOMEN
CT - Abdomen & Pelvis.content:
C.T. SCAN OF ABDOMEN
Known case of acute calculus cholecystitis, post lap assisted open cholecystectomy, with extra hepatic biliary
stricture.
Serial axial sections of the abdomen were studied with oral and I.V.Bolus contrast.
The study shows normal anatomical configuration of the liver with uniform density. No focal or diffuse
pathology is noted.
Well defined collection with enhancing wall measuring approximately 6.8 x 5.9 x 9.1cm (AP x TR x CC) noted in
the right perihepatic space in subcapsular position on right side causing indentation and mass effect of the
underlying liver parenchyma. Mild diffuse thickening of the hepatic capsule is seen in this region.
Irregular shaped thin rim enhancing collection is seen just in the gallbladder fossa region and extends to the
anterior abdominal wall region. Thin collection is also seen in the abutting the anterior peritoneum in this
region with maximum thickness of 9.5 mm.
Mild diffuse thickening of the peritoneum is seen in the right hypochondrial region.
Perihepatic fat stranding noted. Minimal fat stranding is noted adjacent to head of pancreas.
Mild dilatation of the intrahepatic biliary radicles and proximal common hepatic duct noted (measures 10.4 mm
in AP diameter). Abrupt narrowing of the common hepatic duct is seen just beyond its origin. Mild
circumferential thickening of the duct wall is seen, just distal to the stenosis, for a short segment length of
approximately 1.5 cm. The CBD distal to this segment appear normal in wall thickness and shows air within the
lumen, probably secondary to intervention.
Portal and hepatic veins are normal.
Few lymph nodes are seen along the periportal region, largest measuring approximately 11 mm in short axis.
Gall bladder is not visualised, consistent with post-surgical status. Small hyperdense focus is seen in the
gallbladder fossa region, probably postop changes.
Post-operative changes are seen in the anterior abdominal wall on the right side.
The head, body and tail of the pancreas are well demonstrated and are normal in size, shape and attenuation.
Well defined irregularly marginated heterogeneous lesion with soft tissue and fat density measuring 1.6 x 3.4
cm noted in the peripancreatic region anterior to head and neck region of pancreas, possibly fat necrosis.
Few other similar nodules are also seen along the pancreas near the head and uncinate process regions.
The spleen is normal with regard to size, position and morphology and displays uniform enhancement pattern.
Both the kidneys are normal in size, shape and position and show good excretion of contrast with adequate
demonstration of pelvicaliceal system.
Small simple cortical cyst is seen in the interpolar region of right kidney.
Two tiny calculi are seen in the lower polar region left kidney, largest measuring approximately 2.5 mm.
The perinephric area is normal.
The adrenals are normal on both sides.
Aorta, IVC and paraaortic areas are normal. No significant sized retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy noted.
The bowel loops and mesentery are normal.
No significant free fluid seen in the pelvis.
The bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall. No evidence of stone or mass.

LIMITED CT - BREAST
Clinical Indication: Ulcerated right breast mass foe evaluation of left breast.

right breast with extension and infiltration of the overlying skin measuring approximately 7.5 cm in its
maximum dimension. There is also extension of the mass into the retro mammary fat involving the anterior
aspect of the pectoralis muscle. The right nipple is completely destroyed.

discrete enlarged lymph nodes in both axilla with loss of fatty hilum. The largest discrete node measures 2.5 X
1.5 cm on the left side.
IMPRESSION:
Irregular shaped right breast mass with infiltration and ulceration of the skin and enlarged bilateral axillary
nodes.
Highly suggestive of malignancy.

AP) is seen in the superolateral aspect of the right bony orbit, closely associated with adjacent suture. Focal
widening of the suture is seen underneath the lesion. However, no extension to the intra orbital region is

CT - Other.title: CT CORONARY ANGIO
CT - Other.content:
CT CORONARY ANGIO
Clinical features: K/c/o post CABG. C/o chest pain.
Technique:
Axial 0.5 mm thin CT sections were performed through the heart with ECG gating and intravenous non ionic
contrast. Reconstructions were performed through R-R interval in systole and diastole. Three dimensional
multiplanar and curved reconstructions performed through the coronary arteries were studied.
Report:
Grafts:
" LIMA to LAD is patent with good distal opacification.
" SVG to D1 is patent with good distal opacification.
" SVG to last OM is patent. The last OM distal to anastomosis reveals diffuse soft plaques with significant
stenosis in proximal segment.
" SVG to distal RCA is patent with good distal opacification.
Native vessels:
The coronary arterial system is right dominant.
The Left main coronary artery (LMCA) is very short and reveals thick calcified plaques. It bifurcates into
anterior descending (LAD) and left circumflex (LCx).
The proximal and mid LAD reveals diffuse calcified and mixed plaques causing a short segment chronic occlusion
in the mid segment.
The grafted first diagonal artery reveals diffuse calcified plaques proximal to graft anastomosis. The second
diagonal is small and reveals no significant stenosis.
The LCx reveals diffuse mixed plaques and thick soft plaques in the proximal segment causing long segment
critical stenosis. The mid LCx reveals no significant stenosis. The OM1 is small.
The grafted last obtuse marginal (OM) branch reveals soft plaques and is occluded proximal to graft
anastomosis.
The proximal right coronary artery (RCA) reveals predominantly calcified and mixed plaques causing 99 %
stenosis. The mid and distal RCA reveals eccentric soft plaques causing no significant stenosis.
The posterior descending artery (PDA) and posterolateral branch reveals no significant stenosis.
Myocardium reveals mild focal thinning in the mid inferior, inferoseptal, apical septal and anterior walls.
Functional study:
EF : 55 %
EDV : 111 ml
ESV : 49 ml
SV : 62 ml
CO : 4.4 L/min
Myocardial mass : 87 g
IMPRESSION:
" CT coronary angio findings reveal patent LIMA to LAD, SVG to D1 and SVG to distal RCA.
" Patent SVG to last OM with a point of significant stenosis distal to graft anastomosis.
" Native coronary triple vessel disease.
Dr Suresh Kumar R / Dr Pudhiavan A

CT - Thorax & Chest.title: C.T.SCAN OF THORAX AND ABDOMEN

C.T.SCAN OF THORAX AND ABDOMEN
Serial axial sections of the thorax and abdomen were studied after administration of I.V.Bolus contrast.
The study shows normal lung pattern with even distribution of the pulmonary arterial branches and that of the
bronchial tree.
A well-defined heterogenously enhancing soft tissue density mass lesion measuring 11x 10x 7 cm (CCX APX TR) is
seen in the left upper lobe involving both anterior and apical segments. The lesion shows heterogeneous
enhancement and appear hypodense compared to the collapsed lung seen in the periphery of the mass lesion in the
venous phase.
Medially the lesion invades the mediastinal pleura. There is loss of fat plane between the mass and the
posterior half of the arch of aorta and the proximal descending thoracic aorta in its lateral aspect.
The mass encases the proximal left subclavian artery from its origin.
There is also focal loss of fat plane between the mass and the left brachiocephalic vein anteriorly. Antero
inferiorly there is loss of fat plane between the posterior wall of the left pulmonary artery which also shows
mild luminal narrowing.
There of fat in between the oesophagus and the mass is maintained except at D3 level. The masses extending for
more than 4 cm abutting the chest wall both anteriorly and posteriorly.
Minimal paraseptal emphysematous changes are seen in the right apex. Few scattered centriacinar emphysematous
changes are also seen in both lungs.
Subsegmental atelectasis is seen in the basal segments of left lower lobe over the subsegmental collapse
involving the anterior and apical posterior segment of the left upper lobe surrounding the mass lesion.
Few well defined nodules are seen in the anterior basal segment of right upper lobe and posterior segment of
left upper lobe. The largest nodule measures 4.5 mm in the posterior segment of left upper lobe.
Multiple enhancing lymph nodes are noted at prevascular, right paratracheal, left paratracheal, left
para-aortic, sub aortic, pre carinal and at subcarinal levels and bilateral hilar levels. The largest node
measures 1.3 cm at left hilar and subcarinal levels.
There is no pleural effusion seen.
The study shows normal anatomical configuration of the liver with uniform density. No focal or diffuse
pathology is noted.
The intrahepatic biliary radicles, portal and hepatic veins are normal.
The head, body and tail of the pancreas are well demonstrated and are normal in size, shape and attenuation.

There is no free fluid seen in the abdomen.

Large ill-defined heterogeneous enhancing mass lesion in the cervix with extensions as detailed. Features are

MRI - Breast.title: RADIOLOGY REPORT
MRI - Breast.content:
Clinical Indication: Carcinoma left breast, post lumpectomy, radiotherapy and on Letrozole, now MRI showing
right frontal bone metastasis ; for evaluation.
Technique:
Whole body images (vertex to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq of
18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 81mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in region of head and neck.
There is no significant cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the
cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and submandibular glands are unremarkable. No focal mass
lesion/mass effect is seen within the visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of chest.
Psoas left breast lumpectomy status.
No abnormalities are detected in bilateral axilla or internal mammary node.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs, mediastinum and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of abdomen and pelvis.
Liver parenchyma appears normal. Kidneys appear unremarkable. There is no hydroureteronephrosis .The
gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection in
the abdomen and pelvis. There is no significant retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy.
SKELETON:
Multiple intensely hypermetabolic mixed lytic sclerotic lesions noted in right frontal bone, left pubis and
neck of right femur, SUVmax 16.2.
IMPRESSION:
MULTIPLE INTENSELY HYPERMETABOLIC SKELETAL LESIONS; CONSISTENT WITH METASTASIS.
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ELSEWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.
Dr K K Kamaleshwaran MD Dr. E Ramkumar DNB
HOD & Chief Consultant Registrar
Department of NM & PET-CT Department of NM & PET-CT

The right parotid gland is not visualised - history of surgery.

Bilateral submandibular and sublingual glands are normal.
Neck vessels show normal flow signal intensities.

No significant change in size of the lesion noted.

MRI - Obstetrics.title: RADIOLOGY REPORT
MRI - Obstetrics.content:
The overall prognosis of sacrococcygeal teratomas is guarded, with a neonatal mortality rate of 30-40 %; which

output cardiac failure and hydrops.
A follow up after 2 weeks may be recommended to assess the interval increase in size of the tumour and
associated changes.

¢ Well-defined lesion in anterior aspect of neck predominantly on right side, crossing midline and extending to
left side of neck with mass effect on trachea and esophagus as detailed.
¢ Mild polyhydramnios.

Counselling:
Today's scan shows fetal neck mass with airway and esophageal obstruction and mild polyhydramnios as detailed.
Serial scans are required to assess liquor and fetal well being. Delivery has to be planned in a tertiary care
center with pediatric surgical expertise having EXIT (Ex utero Intrapartum Treatment) capability and
specialized neonatal care.
Tracheo-Esophageal Displacement Index (TEDI) < 12 mm indicates low risk of complicated airway at birth.

Singleton live intrauterine gestation with fetus corresponding to 22 weeks 2 days.
Well defined T2 heterointense, T1 hypointense lesion measuring 1.8 x 1.9 x 1.3 cm with cystic areas within is
noted in the anterior mediastinum on the right side. The lesion is abutting the pericardium, main pulmonary
artery and encasing the ascending aorta. No obvious luminal narrowing of great vessels in the present scan.
No diffusion restriction or GRE hypointensities within the lesion.
Superiorly the lesion is noted reaching upto the prevascular space. Inferiorly it is noted abutting the right
hemidiaphragm.
On USG correlation, the lesion appears predominantly hyperechoic with cystic areas. A small vascular pedicle is
noted arising from the ascending aorta supplying the lesion. No calcifications within.
Persistent left SVC is noted draining into dilated coronary sinus.
Fetal brain appears normal.
Kidneys appear normal. No dilatation of pelvicaliceal system noted.
Situs solitus is noted.
Rest of the intra-abdominal organs appear normal in size and signal intensity
The spine is normal.
Evaluation of fetal extremities and heart could not be adequately done due to fetal movement artifacts.
Adequate amniotic fluid is noted.
Placenta is fundal and posterior and the lower margin is well away from the internal os.
The cervix is normal and internal os is closed.
Screening of rest of the maternal abdomen shows normal ovaries and adnexae bilaterally.
Screening of the fetus (on USG correlation) - no other gross congenital anomalies
IMPRESSION:
" Imaging features are suggestive of solid cystic lesion in the anterior mediastinum on right side, more likely
from the pericardium rather than right lung - possibly mediastinal teratoma.
" Persistent left SVC draining into dilated coronary sinus.
Counselling:
Overall prognosis depends on the nature of the lesion, progression of size, mass effect on adjacent mediastinal
structures. Tracheal compression may require immediate neonatal intervention. Vascular compression may result
in hydrops. This condition will require postnatal evaluation and surgery.
Follow up: -
" Suggested pediatric cardiology and pediatric cardiothoracic surgeon opinion.
" Serial follow up scans as recommended.

nerve roots.

The rest of the intervertebral discs are normal in heights and hydration. The vertebral end-plates are normal.

The conus medullaris ends at upper border of L1 and the cauda equine is normal in appearance.

joint arthropathy is noted at C5-C6 level causing bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.

causing mild secondary canal narrowing and indenting bilateral exiting nerve roots.

hyperintense on ST IR sequence measuring 8.5 X 7.3 X 7.1 cm (CC X TR X AP) in the pelvis and is seen between

up to the pubic symphysis.
Left laterally the lesion is extending to the pelvic sidewall with loss of fat plane between the mass and the
obturator internus muscle.
Medially the mass is invading the left half of prostate predominantly the peripheral zone, left seminal
vesical, left lateral wall of the distal rectum and proximal anal canal with invasion of the levator ani muscle
and puborectalis sling. There is also focal invasion of the right seminal vesicle.
Posteriorly the lesion is invading the meso rectal fascia and is seen extending into the nasal rectal fat with
invasion of the anterior and left lateral wall of the distal rectum. A few ill-defined deposits are also noted
in the meso rectal fat.
The lesion is also invading the left distal ureter causing moderate high both ureter.
Few nodes are noted along the superior rectal vessels, the largest measuring 7 mm in short axis diameter. Few
operated nodes are also noted.
Multiple lytic lesions are noted involving the pelvic bones. Some of them have adjacent soft tissue component.
There is obvious destruction of the cortex of the left inferior pubic ramus with adjacent soft tissue and
invasion of the obturator externus muscle.
All these lesions show significant diffusion restriction.
Screening of the whole spine shows focal hyperintense lesion involving the posterior elements of D4, D11-D12
vertebrae and L5 vertebral body. No cord compression.
IMPRESSION:
1. Large ill-defined lesion predominantly in the left side of the pelvis between the bladder and rectum with
invasion of pelvic organs and muscles with pelvic adenopathy as detailed. The exact organ of origin could not
be defined, likely left seminal vesicle/ prostate.

spine.

enhancement.

structures and rectum with grossly preserved fat planes. No defined involvement of rectum is seen.

cm in craniocaudal dimension. Encasement of all the nerve roots in the region of sacral canal involvement.

causing mass effect over bilateral gluteus maximus muscles (R>L) with loss of fat planes at few areas.

preserved fat planes.
No significant size pelvic or lower retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy is seen.

Bilateral hip joints appear normal. No joint effusion or synovial thickening seen.
Rest of the visualized pelvic bones and proximal femurs appear normal.
Rest of the visualized muscles and tendons appear normal.
No abnormal soft tissue inflammation or collection seen.
SI joints: Bilateral sacroiliac joints appear normal for age.

thecal sac/ mild cord indentation are seen at few cervical levels.
Spinal cord shows normal signal intensity. The conus medullaris ends at L1 level and the cauda equine is normal
in appearance.
IMPRESSION:
" Large, well circumscribed lobulated mass lesion in sacrococcygeal region with extensions and mass effect as
detailed. Features are consistent with Chordoma.

Clinical profile: Soft painless swelling over left supraclavicular region and axilla ? lymphangioma.
Technique: IR all planes, T2 axial, T1 axial, T1 fs axial, DWI. Post contrast images - fat sat T1 all three
planes
A large, relatively well defined, lobulated multiseptated cystic lesion measuring approximately 12 x 7 x 6.3 cm
(CC x AP x TR) is seen in the intermuscular plane in the left supraclavicular region, extending to left
anterolateral chest wall and axilla. The lesion appears predominantly iso to hyperintense on T1 and
hyperintense on T2 weighted images.
Multiple fluid-fluid levels are seen within the loculations. Few dependent T1 hyperintensity is seen within the
lesion- possibly hemorrhage/ high protein content. No enhancing solid components are seen within. No foci of
diffusion restriction are seen. On post contrast images, smooth enhancement of septae and walls of the lesion
is seen.
No arterial feeders or prominent draining veins are seen. Mild asymmetrical prominence of left external jugular
vein and left upper limb veins are seen.
Superiorly, the lesion extends upto C5-6 level, and is located posterior to the sternocleidomastoid and
anterior to trapezius. Inferiorly, it extends along the left axilla and anterolateral chest wall upto left 6th
rib level, posterior to the clavicle, left subclavian vessels, pectoralis muscles; and anterior to

unremarkable.
Musculoskeletal System & Spine
Visualized bones show normal marrow signal.

Spinal cord appears normal.
IMPRESSION
o Large heterogeneously enhancing malignant soft-tissue mass in the left lateral neck with internal necrosis,
diffusion restriction, and extension through the widened left C3-C4 neural foramina, associated with mass
effect on adjacent structures.
o Multiple heterogeneously enhancing diffusion-restricting subcutaneous soft-tissue lesions involving the head,
neck, trunk, and extremities, consistent with multifocal disease.
o Small right hilar/mediastinal lymph node (7 × 6 mm), likely metastatic.
o No adrenal or retroperitoneal primary mass identified.
Overall imaging features are suggestive of an aggressive malignant neoplasm with multifocal
soft-tissue/subcutaneous involvement.
Differential considerations include:
1. Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma with multifocal soft-tissue deposits
2. Extra-adrenal neuroblastoma with soft-tissue and nodal metastases
Histopathological correlation and further oncologic evaluation are strongly recommended.
Dr.Aathithya

Technique:
Whole body images (base of skull to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq
of 18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 81mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
Mildly hypermetabolic tiny right supraclavicular lymphnode noted, measuring 5mm with an SUV max of 4.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the head and neck.
Diffuse intense FDG uptake noted in both lobes of the thyroid with an SUV max of 9.2.
The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and
submandibular glands are unremarkable. The mastoid air cells and the paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No
focal mass lesion/mass effect is seen within the visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
Intensely hypermetabolic necrotic right breast lesion with skin infiltration noted, measuring 3.5x3.2cm with an
SUV max of 6.2.
Ametabolic tiny right axillary lymphnode noted measuring 3mm.
Intensely hypermetabolic right paratracheal and precarinal lymphnodes noted , largest measuring 1.5cm with an
SUV max of 5.5. Precarinal lymphnode shows calcification.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the chest.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
Mildly hypermetabolic lobulated solid lesion with cystic component noted involving the pelvis, measuring
12x11x10cm with an SUV max of 4.
Mildly hypermetabolic enhancing peritoneal nodules noted , measuring 1cm with an SUV max of 2.
Mildly hypermetabolic minimal ascites noted in the perihepatic and perisplenic locations with an SUV max of 2.
Ametabolic hypodense noted in the subcapsular location of the segment VII of the liver, measuring 4x2.5cm.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Kidneys appear unremarkable. There is no hydroureteronephrosis. The gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the
adrenals are unremarkable. There is no significant retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy.
SKELETAL:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the extremities and musculo- skeletal system.There is no focal
suspicious lytic or blastic osseous lesion.
IMPRESSION:
INTENSELY HYPERMETABOLIC NECROTIC RIGHT BREAST LESION WITH SKIN INFILTRATION ; CONSISTENT WITH PRIMARY
MALIGNANCY.
HYPERMETABOLIC RIGHT SUPRACLAVICULAR AND MEDIASTINAL LYMPHNODES ; NEEDS HPE CORRELATION TO RULE OUT METASTASES.
MILDLY HYPERMETABOLIC LOBULATED SOLID LESION WITH CYSTIC COMPONENT NOTED INVOLVING THE PELVIS ; COULD BE SECOND
PRIMARY OVARIAN MALIGNANCY.
MILDLY HYPERMETABOLIC PERITONEAL NODULES AND ASCITES ; CONSISTENT WITH METASTASES.
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ELSEWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.

Nuclear Medicine - Breast.content:
Clinical Indication: - Ca left breast; for staging evaluation.
Technique:
Whole body images (base of skull to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq
of 18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 115mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the head and neck.
There is no significant cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the
cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and submandibular glands are unremarkable. The mastoid
air cells and the paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No focal mass lesion/mass effect is seen within the
visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
Intensely hypermetabolic heterogeneously enhancing necrotic soft tissue lesion noted in lower outer quadrant of
the left breast measuring 4.3x4cm with an SUV max of 23.1.
Mildly hypermetabolic skin thickening noted in left breast adjacent to the lesion with an SUV max of 3.8.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the chest.
Ametabolic tiny enhancing left level I axillary lymphnodes noted, measuring 6mm.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs, mediastinum and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Liver parenchyma appears normal. Kidneys appear unremarkable. There is no hydroureteronephrosis .The
gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection
in the abdomen and pelvis. There is no significant retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy.
SKELETAL:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the extremities and musculo- skeletal system. There is no focal
suspicious lytic or blastic osseous lesion.
IMPRESSION:
INTENSELY HYPERMETABOLIC HETEROGENEOUSLY ENHANCING NECROTIC SOFT TISSUE LESION NOTED IN LOWER OUTER QUADRANT OF
THE LEFT BREAST; CONSISTENT WITH PRIMARY MALIGNANCY.
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ELSEWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.

Stress and Rest Myocardial Perfusion Scintigraphy
Stress SPECT myocardial perfusion scintigraphy was performed after intravenous injection of standard dose of
Tc99m Sestamibi. Physical stress was performed on a Tread Mill using Modified Bruce Protocol.

Stress Parameters:
Duration of Exercise : 11:21min (7.0Mets)
Baseline Heart Rate and BP : 65 / min, 140/90 mm Hg
Maximum Heart Rate Achieved : 108 / min, <85% of MPHR
Maximum Blood Pressure : 160/80 mm Hg
ECG Changes : Nil
Findings:
LV cavity appears normal in size in post stress and rest images.
No tracer uptake is seen in lungs and right ventricle.
Stress and rest perfusion images(qualitative analysis):
Small sized area of severe grade fixed perfusion defect noted in apex and apicoanterior segment.
Rest of the segments of myocardium demonstrate normal perfusion
Functional evaluation with Gated SPECT:
Normal LV function at stress and rest.
Apex and apical anterior demonstrates hypokinetic with reduced wall thickening
Rest of segments of myocardium demonstrates normal wall thickening and wall motion.
BULL'S EYE EVALUATION:
Summed stress score (SSS) is 6 (demonstrates ischemia or infarct).
Summed rest score (SRS) is 6 (demonstrates scar or infarct)
Summed difference score (SDS) is 0 (ischemia globally)
SCORING AND QUALITATIVE DEFINITIONS FOLLOWED IN THE REPORTING FORMAT:
Cumulative scores are taken from all 17 segments at stress and rest.
17 segments are scored from 0 to 4 with 0 = normal perfusion, 1= mild decrease in perfusion, 2 = moderate
decrease in perfusion, 3 =severe decrease in perfusion and 4 = absent perfusion).
Defect size classification:
Small: equal to or less than 2 segments, moderate size: 3 or 4 segments; large size is > 4 segments involved.
The perfusion defect size may be quantitatively described as small, medium or large. Small defect represents
less than 10%, medium 10-20% and large represents greater than or equal 20% of the LV myocardium.
Defect severity classification:
Mild grade: not normal but > 70 % perfusion maintained
Moderate grade: 50-70 % perfusion maintained
Severe grade: 30-50 % perfusion maintained.
Absent perfusion: less than 30 % perfusion maintained. This scoring is also used in Bulls Eye evaluation.

Stress SPECT myocardial perfusion scintigraphy was performed after intravenous injection of standard dose of
Tc99m Sestamibi. Physical stress was performed using modified Bruce Protocol on treadmill.
Stress Parameters:
Duration of Exercise : 08.17min (4.6Mets)
Baseline Heart Rate and BP : 92/ min, 170/90 mm Hg
Maximum Heart Rate Achieved : 100/ min, (<85% of MPHR)
Maximum Blood Pressure : 170/90mm of Hg
ECG Changes : Nil
Cause of termination : Fatigue
Complaints : Nil.
Findings:
The LV cavity appears normal in size in the post stress images.
No tracer uptake is seen in lungs and right ventricle.
Stress perfusion images (qualitative analysis):
All segments of myocardium demonstrate normal perfusion at stress
Functional evaluation with Gated SPECT:
Normal LVEF at stress.
All segments of the myocardium demonstrate normal wall motion and normal thickening.
BULL'S EYE EVALUATION:
Summed stress score (SSS) is 0 (demonstrates ischemia or infarct)
SCORING AND QUALITATIVE DEFINITIONS FOLLOWED IN THE REPORTING FORMAT:
Cumulative scores are taken from all 17 segments at stress and rest.
17 segments are scored from 0 to 4 with 0 = normal perfusion, 1= mild decrease in perfusion, 2 = moderate
decrease in perfusion, 3 =severe decrease in perfusion and 4 = absent perfusion).
Defect size classification:
Small: equal to or less than 2 segments, moderate size: 3 or 4 segments; large size is > 4 segments involved.
The perfusion defect size may be quantitatively described as small, medium or large. Small defect represents
less than 10%, medium 10-20% and large represents greater than or equal 20% of the LV myocardium.
Defect severity classification:
Mild grade: not normal but > 70 % perfusion maintained
Moderate grade: 50-70 % perfusion maintained
Severe grade: 30-50 % perfusion maintained.
Absent perfusion: less than 30 % perfusion maintained.
This scoring is also used in Bulls Eye evaluation.
The defect severity is expressed visually as mild, moderate or severe. A mild defect is identified by a
decrease count compared to the adjacent wall with preserved thickness, moderate defect demonstrate wall
thinning and severe defect appears similar to background activity.

Nuclear Medicine - Trauma & Whole Body.title: PET CT whole body.
Nuclear Medicine - Trauma & Whole Body.content:
PET CT whole body.
Brain: Age-related parenchymal changes noted.
Left parotid gland: Two enhancing focal lesions noted, measuring about 3.3 X 3.3 cm and 1.8 X 1.4 centimetre.
The largest lesion shows a few nonenhancing areas within - may represent necrosis/cystic changes. Needs
histopathology correlation.
Thorax:
Areas of fibro cavitating lesions is noted in bilateral upper lobe (right more than left). Tiny calcified
granuloma is noted in the apical segment of the right upper lobe. Collapse with bronchiectasis is seen
involving the right upper lobe.
Scattered areas of centriacinar and paraseptal emphysematous changes noted in both lungs.
Areas of subsegmental atelectasis is also noted in the right middle lobe and lingular segment of left upper
lobe.
Few lymph nodes are noted in the right paratracheal and subcarinal region, the largest measuring about 9 mm in
short axis.
Aorta - diffuse atherosclerotic changes noted. 2.3 X 2.3 cm sized inferolaterally projecting saccular aneurysm
is noted from mid-portion of the aortic arch.
Rest of the descending thoracic aorta and upper abdominal aorta is ectatic.
An infrarenal aortic aneurysm measuring about 6 cm craniocaudally is noted. Transaxial measurements of the
aneurysm is 4.3 X 4.2 cm. Part of aneurysm is thrombosed, with patent lumen trans axially measures about 3.3 X
2.8 cm.
Abdomen:
Liver - is shrunken with nodular margins consistent with cirrhosis. The main portal vein show cavernamtous
transformation. A mass lesion measuring about 4X 3.8 cm is noted in inferior segment of right lobe of liver
which enhances in arterial phase and show washout in venous phase - consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma.
Few subcentimetre sized hypodense lesion is noted in both lobes of liver - may represent regenerative nodules,
suggested MRI for further evaluation if indicated.
Spleen - normal in size, splenorenal collaterals noted.
Few simple exophytic cortical cyst noted in right kidney, the largest measuring about 1.3 X 1.2 cm.
Right-sided inguinal hernia with small bowel loops as its content is noted.

ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:

gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection

Head:

parenchyma is normal.
Neck:
There is a lytic lesion with soft tissue component involving the ramus of the mandible on the left side
measuring 3.4 X 3.1 cm.
Chest:
There is air space opacity and consolidation involving the superior lingula segment of the upper lobe.
Abdomen:
There is a heterogeneously enhancing lesion measuring 3.3 X 2.9 cm in the region of right adrenal gland. The
right adrenal gland is not separately seen.
There is a heterogeneously enhancing lesion measuring 1.4 X 1.6 cm in the lateral limb of the left adrenal
gland.
There is nodular enhancing lesions seen along the right crura adjacent the operated site. The largest nodule
measures 1.3 cm.
Right nephrectomy status noted.
Left moderate hydrosalphinx is noted.

Unknown_Modality - Abdomen & Pelvis.title: ABDOMEN
Unknown_Modality - Abdomen & Pelvis.content:
ABDOMEN
The study shows normal anatomical configuration of the liver with uniform density. The left lateral segment is
atrophic. A well defined hypodense non enhancing cyst is seen in segment 6 measuring 11 mm. A focus of
calcification is seen in segment 7 of liver.
Two CBD stents are seen in situ. The intrahepatic biliary radicles are not dilated.
Few enhancing nodes are seen at the root of mesentery with largest measuring 10 mm in SAD.
The head, body and tail of the pancreas are well demonstrated and are normal in size, shape and attenuation.
The gall bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall. No evidence of any stone, sludge or mass.
The spleen is normal with regard to size, position and morphology.
Both the kidneys are normal in size, shape and position. The perinephric area is normal.
The adrenals are normal on both sides.
Aorta, IVC and paraaortic areas are normal. No retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy noted.
The bowel loops and mesentery are normal.
Few enhancing nodular deposits are seen in the peritoneum in the recto vesicle pouch. Similar enhancing nodules
are also seen in the omentum. There is no free fluid seen in the abdomen.
The bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall. No evidence of stone or mass.
BONES
No suspicious lytic/sclerotic lesions in the visualized bones.
IMPRESSION: Compared to previous PET CT, there is increase in the size and number of the peritoneal and omental
nodules.

BRAIN
The sections of the brain do not reveal any area of altered tissue density.

The ventricular system shows normal anatomical configuration.
There is no midline shift seen.
The basal cisterns, cortical sulci and sylvian fissures are normal.
The sella, parasellar and suprasellar regions are normal.
Bones of cranial vault are normal.
NECK
Nasopharynx, oropharynx and hypopharynx are normal.
Larynx is normal.
Bilateral submandibular and parotid gland are normal.
No evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy.
Thyroid gland is normal.
Neck vessels are normal.
Trachea and visualized portion of esophagus are normal.
THORAX
The study shows normal lung pattern with even distribution of the pulmonary arterial branches and that of the
bronchial tree.
The anatomical configuration of the structures in the mediastinum and both hilar regions are normal.
There is no evidence of hilar lymphadenopathy seen.
The arch of the aorta and the vessels arising from it are normal.
There is no evidence of pleural effusion seen.
ABDOMEN
There are focal hypo dense lesions in both lobes of the liver. The lesion measures 2 cm in segment 7 of right
lobe of liver. There is another ill-defined hypo dense lesion measuring approximately 1.5 x 1.5 x 2.5 cm (AP X
TR X CC) in segment 4 of left lobe of liver closely abutting the middle hepatic vein and the left hepatic duct
region. There is intrahepatic biliary radicle dilatation involving the left lobe of liver. The lateral segments
of left lobe also show diffuse heterogeneous density suggestive o infiltrative pathology. Also there is a focal
sub capsular hypo dense lesion measuring 1cm in segment 3.
Few peripancreatic lymph nodes are seen measuring 6 mm.

Unknown_Modality - Brain & Head.content:

No evidence of any stone, sludge or mass.

Both the kidneys are normal in size, shape and position.
The perinephric area is normal.
The adrenals are normal on both sides.
Aorta, IVC are normal.
The bowel loops and mesentery are normal.
There is no free fluid seen in the abdomen.
The bladder is well distended and displays mild diffuse wall thickening. No evidence of stone or mass.
The prostate is enlarged in size. TURP defect noted within the gland.
Both the seminal vesicles could not be separately made out.
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are noted along bilateral external iliac, internal iliac and right common iliac
arteries, largest node measuring 1.6 cm along the right common iliac artery.
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes are noted in the retrocaval, para-aortic, preaortic and aortocaval locations
largest node measuring 1.2 cm in short axis
BONES
Sclerotic lesion noted in body of these six vertebra.
Mild increase in trabecular density noted in the left acetabulum in the region of uptake on PET CT.
Diffuse degenerative changes of spine are seen.
IMPRESSION: Patient known case of carcinoma prostate; status post orchidectomy and radiotherapy. Now
presenting with increasing serum PSA levels.
1. Enlarged prostate with possible involvement of the bilateral seminal vesicles - consistent with primary.
2. Retroperitoneal and iliac lymphadenopathy as detailed - metastatic.
3. Sclerotic lesions in bone - metastatic.
4. Diffuse bladder wall thickening - probably post obstructive.
3. Age-related cortical atrophy of brain.
Dr.Sumathi

Unknown_Modality - Extremities & Joints.content:
Clinical features- left foot fourth toe gangrenous changes.
LEFT LOWER LIMB ANGIOGRAPHY
Through left CFA 4F access, aortic bifurcation CO2 angiogram showed normal aortic bifurcation, with normal
bilateral common iliac, external iliac, internal iliac and bilateral common femoral arteries.
Left profunda femoris artery and its branches were normal.
Left common femoral artery injection showed normal superficial femoral artery with no significant stenosis and
good forward flow. The left popliteal artery was normal.
Left anterior tibial artery showed occlusion of mid segment with no distal reformation with presence of
multiple parallel collaterals which are seen continuing into the foot.
Tibioperoneal trunk is normal. Multiple tandem stenosis in the proximal segment and occlusion of the mid
segment of the peroneal artery with no distal reformation
Multiple tandem stenosis of the entire posterior tibial artery with occlusion just above the ankle with
multiple collaterals continuing into the foot.
Right CFA Sheath was removed and puncture site hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total fluoroscopic time: 6min
Total Radiation dose: 106mGy
CONCLUSION:
o Left anterior tibial artery showed occlusion of mid segment with no distal reformation with multiple parallel
collaterals
o Multiple tandem stenosis in the proximal segment and occlusion of the mid segment of the peroneal artery with
no distal reformation
o Multiple tandem stenosis of the entire posterior tibial artery with occlusion just above the ankle with
multiple collaterals continuing into the foot.
In view of poor distal outflow, none of the vessels amenable for endovascular intervention.

PATIENT NAME: MR.RAVICHANDRAN ID NO.: 1687618
AGE : 55 YEARS DATE : 18.02.2021.
RIGHT BELOW KNEE ANGIOPLASTY
Clinical Profile: Non healing ulcer right great toe amputation stump and dorsum of foot.
Under local anesthesia with strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's technique, left common
femoral artery was accessed and secured with 4F short sheath. Through left CFA access CO2 angiograms of aortic
bifurcation and right lower limb were done. It revealed normal bilateral common, internal, external iliac
arteries, bilateral common femoral, right superficial femoral, right popliteal arteries .
ATA showed patent proximal ostium and proximal stump with occlusion for a length of 58 mm with multi focal high
grade tandem stenosis (80-90%) in the mid third. There was reformation of distal ATA & DPA through collaterals.
DPA formed the plantar arch.
The proximal tibio-peroneal trunk was normal with short segment occlusion of the distal TP trunk and proximal
peroneal artery. The mid and distal peroneal artery showed good forward flow. The PTA showed diffuse disease in
the proximal segment with occlusion of middle and distal third.
Using fluoroscopic guidance, antegrade access was obtained in the right common femoral artery and 45 cm long 5F
sheath was placed in distal right superficial femoral artery. Using a combination of 5 Fr multipurpose
catheter, progreat microcatheter and command 0.014 microwire, the ATA was intubated and occlusion was crossed.
Another 0.014 command wire was simultaneously placed in the peroneal artery and the occlusion was crossed.The
diseased segment of ATA , peroneal and tibio peroneal trunk were dilated using 2-2.5 mm amphirion tapering
plain angioplasty balloon. Post angioplasty angiogram showed small flow limiting dissection in the proximal
anterior tibial artery which was treated with prolonged balloon inflation. Check angiogram showed persistence
of the dissection flap and was treated with 2.5 x 24 mm ultimaster sirolimus drug eluting stent. The
tibioperoneal trunk and proximal peroneal artery were angioplastied with 2-2.5 mm amphirion tapering plain
balloon.
Post procedure angiogram showed good forward flow in the treated vessels with no significant residual stenosis.
Bilateral femoral puncture site hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 290mGy.
Total fluoroscopic time: 29 mins.
CONCLUSION:
Occlusion of proximal right anterior tibial artery - treated successfully by plain balloon angioplasty and
stenting of small dissection.
Short segment occlusion in distal tibioperoneal trunk and proximal peroneal artery-treated successfully by
plain balloon angioplasty.
Chronic occlusion of right mid and distal posterior artery - not amenable to endovascular interventions.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH P

DIAGNOSTIC CEREBRAL ANGIOGRAPHY
Clinical profile: Right MCA infarct. MRA- right MCA stenosis and right ICA top aneurysm.
Under local anesthesia with strict aseptic precautions and using Modified Seldinger's technique, right CFA was
accessed and secured with 4F short sheath.
Using 4F Bernstein catheter, bilateral common carotid, left vertebral angiograms and spin angiogram of right
ICA were done.
It revealed a long segment high grade critical ~90-95% stenosis of cavernous segment of right ICA. There is a
wide necked complex, multilobulated saccular aneurysm seen in ophthalmic segment of right ICA measuring
5.6x3.9mm(FXH) with neck measuring 5.4mm.
Bilateral MCA shows ICAD changes with multifocal mild stenosis.
Right ACA is filling through anterior communicating artery. Right A1 is aplastic.
Bilateral vertebral areteries and basilar artery shows ICAD changes with multifocal moderate grade stenosis.
Parenchymal and venous phases were normal.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 351 mGy.
Total fluoroscopic time: 11.5 min.
CONCLUSION:
Cerebral DSA revealed
" High grade critical ~90-95% stenosis of cavernous segment ICA.
" Wide necked complex, multi-lobulated saccular aneurysm seen in ophthalmic segment of right ICA.
ADVICE : Angioplasty of right cavernous ICA followed by parent artery reconstruction using flow diverter.

AGE : 48 YEARS / MALE DATE : 28.12.23.
SMA AND CELIAC ARTERY ANGIOGRAPHY AND EMBOLISATION OF BLEEDER
Clinical history : C/o acute necrotizing pancreatitis with serial drop in hemoglobin. CT revealed active
contrast extravasation from gastroduodenal artery.
Under strict aseptic precautions, right common femoral artery was accessed and secured using 5F Ansel sheath.
Celiac artery was intubated with 4F yashiro catheter. Following celiac angiogram, Yashiro catheter was
exchanged for Berenstein catheter and superselectrive angiograms of the gastroduodenal artery were performed
using Asahi microcatheter.
It showed active contrast extravasation from posterior superior pancreatico duodenal branch. The culprit artery
was cannulated and embolized with 18-7-2 Nester microcoil, across the neck of the pseudoaneurysm.
Check angiogram revealed no angiographic evidence of active contrast extravasation or pseudoaneurysm or
abnormal vascular blush.
5F Ansel sheath was exchanged for 5F short sheath and sutured in position.
Total radiation dose: 5076 mGy.
Total fluoroscopy time: 14 mins.
CONCLUSION:
Lower GI bleed with active contrast extravasation from gastroduodenal artery branch- treated successfully by
coil embolization.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH P

BRONCHIAL ARTERY EMBOLISATION
Clinical profile: Hemoptysis; CT revealed hypertrophied bronchial arteries.
Under all aseptic precautions and local anesthesia, right common femoral artery was accessed by modified
Seldinger technique and access was secured using 4F sheath.
Using 4F Judgkins Left catheter left bronchial artery and right common bronchial trunck were cannulated.
Angiogram showed abnormal hypertrophic tortuous artery with increased parenchymal blush. The culprit artery
were embolized with 300-500 microns PVA particles.
Post-embolization injection showed obliteration of the hypertrophied vessel with sluggish forward flow.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total fluoroscopic time: 17.5 min.
Total Radiation dose: 443 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Case of hemoptysis- left bronchial and right common bronchial arteries successfully embolized using 300-500 PVA
particles.

Unknown_Modality - Extremities & Joints.content:
Right knee joint Genicular artery embolisation for hemarthrosis (16.04.26)
Clinical profile : S/P TKR with right knee recurrent hemarthosis.
Under strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's technique, right common femoral artery was
accessed and secured with 4F cm short sheath.
Using 4F Berenstein catheter popliteal angiogram was taken. It revealed normal left superficial femoral and
popliteal arteries. There was increased vascular blush along the lateral aspect of knee joint supplied by
lateral superior genicular artery and along the medial aspect of knee joint supplied by articular branch of
descending genicular artery.
These were selectively cannulated using Merit Maestro microcatheter and Truform microwire and were
subsequently embolised by 300-500 PVA until pruning.
Check angiogram showed resolution of abnormal vascular blush with normal filing of other branches.
Common femoral sheath was removed and hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 2879 mGy
Total fluoroscopy time: 36.4 mins
CONCLUSION:
Case of right knee joint hemarthrosis, angiography showed increased vascular blush along the medial and lateral
aspect of knee joint - treated successfully by superselective embolization of descending genicular , and
lateral superior genicular arteries.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN/DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / .P

INTENSELY HYPERMETABOLIC SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS THICKENING NOTED ADJACENT TO THE AMPUTATION SITE IN THE LEFT

PATIENT NAME : MRS.RATHNA AGE : 42YRS/ FEMALE
DATE : 9/12/19.
BALLON ASSISTED COILING OF ACOM ANEURYSM
Under strict aseptic precautions and general anesthesia, right common femoral artery was accessed by modified
Seldinger's technique and access was secured using 4F short sheath.
Right common carotid artery angiogram and 3D spin were performed, which revealed a wide neck (2.89 mm) saccular
aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery directed superiorly measuring 4.6 x 2.65 mm. Right MCA, right ACA
and their branches were normal. Left ACA was seen filling through ACOM.
Cross-compression left CCA angiogram revealed left A1 filling the aneurysm.
4 F short sheath was exchanged with a 7F 70 cm long sheath with tip positioned at the bifurcation of right CCA.
6F Neuron guiding catheter was positioned in the distal petrous ICA. Using Asahi 014 microwire, Sceptre XC 4 x
11 mm balloon was positioned across the neck of aneurysm with distal end of balloon in left A2. Using Headway
17 microcatheter and Tracess ex microwire, the aneurysm was intubated. Balloon assisted coiling was performed
using detachable neurocoils- 360 Ultra 3 x 6 mm and 360 Ultra 2 x 4 mm.
Post coiling check angiogram revealed complete obliteration of the aneurysm with no e/o residual filling in the
aneurysmal sac.
Puncture site hemostasis achieved by manual compression.
Total Fluroscopic time: 66.8 min.
Total Radiation dose: 2131 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
A wide neck saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery - treated successfully with balloon assisted
coiling.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN /DR.PANKAJ MEHTA/. P

Unknown_Modality - Other.content:
LEFT ICA PARENT ARTERY RECONSTRUCTION WITH FLOW DIVERTER
Clinical profile: case of left supraopthalmic ICA wide neck aneurysm S/P balloon assisted coiling with residual
filling of base of aneurysm.
Under general anesthesia with strict aseptic precautions and using Modified Seldinger's technique, right common
femoral artery was accessed and secured with 4F short sheath.
Using combination of Bernstein catheter and angled terumo guide wire, bilateral common carotid angiogram and
ICA angiogram were acquired.
Tortuous course with irregular beaded appearance of short segments of bilateral cervical ICA were seen - likely
fibro muscular dysplasia.
Right ICA injection with cross compression revealed good flow across Acom into the left ACA and left MCA
without significant venous delay.
Left ICA angiogram revealed compaction of coil mass at the fundus of coiled paraopthalmic ICA aneurysm with
residual filling of base of the aneurysm, measuring approx. 4.5 x 3 mm. Rest of bilateral common carotid, ICA
and its branches appeared normal.
4F short sheath was exchanged with Infinity 80 cm long sheath with its tip positioned in left ICA proximal to
the loop. CAT 5 was positioned in distal petrous ICA. A combination of XT-27 microcatheter and Synchro
microwire was navigated across the neck of aneurysm into M1 segment of left MCA.
Parent artery reconstruction of left ICA was performed with deployment of 4.5 x 25 mm Surpass Evolve flow
diverter across the neck of the aneurysm with distal end in the communicating segment and the proximal end in
the proximal cavernous ICA.
Post procedure check angiogram(immediate and 20 mins delayed) and Dyna CT revealed, good flow across the flow
diverter into the left ACA and MCA without any filling defects. Good apposition of flow diverter with the
vessel wall was seen.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by proglide device.
Total radiation dose: 1977 mGy.
Total fluoroscopic time: 54.7 min.
CONCLUSION:
Case of left supraopthalmic ICA ruptured wide neck aneurysm S/P balloon assisted coiling with residual filling
of base of aneurysm - successfully treated with parent artery reconstruction using Surpass Evolve flow diverter
DR. MATHEW CHERIAN / DR. PANKAJ MEHTA /

CLINICAL PROFILE: - Critical limb ischemia- Right second and third toe healed ulcers with third toe gangrene
RIGHT LOWER LIMB ANGIOGRAPHY & BELOW KNEE ANGIOPLASTY
Under strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's techinique, left common femoral artery was
accessed secured with 5F short sheath.
Angiograms revealed normal right superficial femoral artery, right profunda femoris artery and its branches
were normal. Popliteal artery and its trifurcation were normal.
Below knee angiogram showed tandem stenosis of tibioperoneal trunk and proximal PTA with PTA forming the
predominant run off of foot. Proximal two third of ATA appears normal with occlusion of distal one third.
Proximal peroneal artery appears normal with occlusion of mid two third of peroneal artery and reformation of
distal peroneal artery through collateral from ATA. DPA was reformed through multiple collaterals from ATA and
reformed peroneal artery with significant multifocal disease. Third digital artery showed occlusion at the base
of the toe.
5F short sheath exchanged for 5F 70cm sheath. The stenosis in tibioperoneal trunk and PTA were crossed using
combination of progreat microcatheter- Command 014 wire and exchanged for V18 wire. Proximal PTA was dilated
with 2 X 120mm PTA balloon. Tibioperoneal trunk was serially dilated with 2.5mm and 3mm PTA balloon.
Post procedure angiography showed good flow across the tibioperoneal trunk and PTA into foot with adequate
wound blush of the diseased site. No significant residual stenosis or flow limiting dissection.
Left common femoral sheath was removed and hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 419mGy
Total fluroscopy time: 27mins
CONCLUSION:
Case of critical limb ischemia - Multifocal stenosis in tibioperoneal trunk and PTA with PTA forming the
predominant run off of foot -treated successfully by plain balloon angioplasty.
Distal ATA and mid peroneal artery occlusion as detailed with poor distal outflow - not amenable for
endovascular intervention.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.P.SANTHOSH

DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY OF LEFT THORACIC WALL VASCULAR MALFORMATION
Under aseptic precautions, through right CFA access left subclavian artery was intubated and angiogram taken
which showed a mixed vascular malformation predominantly venous, with tiny arterio-venous fistulae in one of
the sacs being fed by the branches of lateral thoracic artery. Venous drainage was seen into the tributaries of
axillary and subclavian veins.
INTERVENTION
Using Bernstein catheter lateral thoracic artery was embolised with Gelfoam scrapings until stasis was
achieved.
Prominent venous sacs were cannulated with scalp vein set(22G) at 2 sites and 4 ml sclerosant (1 part
lipiodol, 1 part of air and 2 parts of Setrol) was injected after compressing the draining vein.
Total Fluroscopic time: 15.7 min
Total Radiation dose: 230.5 mGy
IMPRESSION:
Mixed type of vascular malformation-1st sitting of treatment performed by gelfoam embolization of lateral
thoracic feeders and STS sclerotherapy of the venous sacs.

LEFT LOWER LIMB ANGIOGRAPHY & BELOW KNEE ANGIOPLASTY
Under strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's technique, right common femoral artery was
accessed and secured with 4F short sheath. Carbon dioxide angiogram of aortic bifurcation and left lower limb
were obtained using a 4F Bernstein catheter.
Angiograms revealed normal aortic bifurcation and the bilateral iliac arteries. The left common femoral,
superficial femoral, deep femoral and popliteal artery were normal.
ATA showed moderate short segment stenosis in the proximal part and multifocal high grade stenosis of the mid
segment. Distal ATA and Dorsalis pedis artery were normal. The tibioperoneal trunk showed mild stenosis.
Short segment occlusion was seen in proximal peroneal artery with multifocal high grade stenosis in mid and
distal third. There was chronic occlusion of the posterior tibial artery with short segment distal reformation
at the ankle through the peroneal artery.
The high grade stenosis in ATA was crossed with a combination of progreat microcatheter and 0.014" Command wire
and dilated using a 3 x 150 mm plain balloon (Coyote).
Short segment proximal occlusion and multifocal high grade stenosis of peroneal artery were dilated with an
Amphiron 2-2.5 x 210mm balloon over a synchro wire.
The tibioperoneal stenosis was dilated using a 3.5 x 60 mm plain balloon (Coyote).
Post procedure angiogram good distal flow in the left anterior tibial artery. Peroneal artery showed sluggish
flow in the distal third.
Sheath was removed and hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 315.3 mGy
Total fluoroscopy time: 46.8 mins
CONCLUSION:
High grade steno-occlusive disease of the left anterior tibial artery and peroneal artery successfully treated
with plain balloon angioplasty.
Chronic occlusion of the left posterior tibial artery: not amenable to endovascular intervention.

RIGHT LOWER LIMB ANGIOGRAM AND RIGHT COMMON ILIAC ARTERY STENTING
Clinical features: Right forefoot pain and blisters in toes. MR angiogram revealed high grade stenosis of the
right common iliac artery.
Under local anesthesia with strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's technique left CFA was
accessed and secured with 4F short sheath.
Through left CFA 4F access, bifurcation CO2 aortogram followed by iodinated contrast was performed using a 4F
berenstein catheter. It revealed multifocal short segment stenosis of proximal right common iliac artery. Left
common iliac artery, bilateral internal and external iliac arteries, bilateral common femoral arteries were
normal. Intra arterial pressure gradient measured across right common iliac artery stenosis was about 40 mm of
Hg. (Mean arterial pressure).
The right common iliac artery stenosis was crossed using an angled Terumo wire and Bernstein catheter and right
lower limb angiograms were taken. The angiogram revealed small calibre normal right superficial femoral artery,
popliteal artery, anterior tibial artery and dorsalis pedis artery. Tibioperoneal trunk was occluded with
reformation of mid and distal posterior tibial artery and peroneal artery.
The short sheath was exchanged for a 7F crossover sheath. Over an extra stiff wire across the right common
iliac artery stenosis, a self expanding stent (EPIC 8mm x 80 mm) was deployed in the right common iliac artery,
across the stenotic segment.
The stent was post dilated with a 5 x 40 mm ( Mustang) balloon.
Post-procedure angiogram revealed good flow across the stent distally without any residual narrowing or flow
limiting dissection. Intra-arterial pressure gradient measured across right common iliac artery stent decreased
to about 10 mm of Hg. (Mean arterial pressure).
Total fluroscopic time: 18 min.
Total Radiation dose: 2075 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Right common iliac artery multifocal stenosis - treated successfully with self expanding stent.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH.P.

ENDOVACULAR BALLOON ASSISTED COILING OF BASILAR ARTERY TOP ANEURYSM
Right common femoral artery was accessed by single wall puncture technique and access was secured using 4F
sheath by modified Seldinger technique.
Bilateral common carotid injection demonstrated normal bilateral intracranial internal carotid artery, anterior
cerebral artery, middle cerebral artery and their branches.
Left Vertebral artery injection showed saccular basilar artery top aneurysm measuring 5.2 mm x 4.4 mm in size
(Dome x Height) with a wide neck (3.8mm).
V4 segment of bilateral vertebral arteries, bilateral anterior and posterior inferior cerebellar arteries,
bilateral superior cerebellar and posterior cerebellar arteries were normal.
The short sheath was exchanged with 7F long sheath which was placed in left subclavian artery. 6F Neuron
guiding catheter was placed in distal portion of V2 segment of vertebral artery.
The aneurysm sac was intubated using a combination of headway 17 Micro catheter and Traxcess- EX guide wire.
Further Scepter-XC 4 x 11 mm balloon was deployed across the aneurysm neck into the right posterior cerebral
artery P1 segment. The aneurysm sac was obliterated using 21 cms of detachable coils (4mm x 13cm Optima complex
soft coil, 3mm x 6 cm Optima Helical supersoft coil and 1 mm x 2 cm 360 Target nano coil).
Post procedure angio showed no filling of the aneurysm and normal filling of vertebro-basilar circulation.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by proglide suture device.
Total radiation dose: 5174mGy.
Total fluroscopic time: 19.2mins.
ONCLUSION:
" Basilar artery top aneurysm successfully treated with endovascular balloon assisted coiling.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH.P.

Clinical profile: Right lower limb (lower thigh and calf) and plantar aspect of foot claudication pain.
Under SAP, under local anaesthesia, left CFA was accessed with 4 F short sheath and angiograms of aortic
bifurcation and right lower limb taken.
It revealed normal bilateral common, external and internal iliac arteries.
Right CFA was normal. Right SFA was occluded beyond a short proximal stump with recanalisation of distal SFA.
Popliteal artery was normal and continued as ATA with single vessel run off into the foot as DPA reforming the
pedal arch. Tibio peroneal trunk, peroneal artery and PTA occluded without reformation.
4F sheath exchanged for 6F 45cm cross over sheath with tip in CFA. The occlusion was crossed subintimally with
straight Terumo wire and Bernstein catheter with re-entry in distal SFA. It was angioplastied with 5 x 200mm
plain balloon (Mustang). The angioplastied segment was stented with 2 overlapping self expanding stents
-supera 5.5x180 and ivolution 6x200mm.

segment without residual stenosis.
Hemostasis achieved by manual compression.

Right SFA long segment occlusion-treated successfully with two overlapping stents (Supera and Ivolution).

MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY FOR RIGHT DISTAL MCA OCCLUSION-ACUTE STROKE
Clinical profile: Acute onset left upper and lower limb weakness and left side lower facial weakness. MRI
revealed occlusion of distal M1 segment of right middle cerebral artery with DWI ASPECT-7.
Under general anesthesia with all aseptic precautions, through right common femoral artery 4F short sheath was
positioned via modified Seldinger's technique. Using 4F Bernstein's catheter angiogram of right common carotid
artery was performed which revealed normal ECA and its branches, ICA and ACA. Right M1 segment of MCA was
occluded. Bernstein's catheter was progressed into the right ECA. The terumo guide wire was exchanged for an
extra stiff wire.
The 4F short sheath was exchanged for a 8 F short sheath. AXS Infinity long sheath (6F, 90 cm) was navigated
into proximal petrous ICA. A Triaxial system of React 71, Phenom 21 microcatheter and Traxcess guidewire was
placed in the right MCA. React 71 was placed in proximal M1 MCA. The combination of Phenom 21 microcatheter and
Traxcess microwire was navigated across the MCA occlusion and stent retrieval device Solitaire 6 x 40 mm was
deployed across the occlusion.
Using modified solumbra technique, two attempts of mechanical thrombectomy failed to recanalise right MCA.
Third attempt of mechanical thrombectomy done by suction aspiration through React 71 aspiration catheter placed
in distal right MCA also failed to recanalise right M1 MCA. Final attempt of mechanical thrombectomy was done
by modified solumbra technique with Embotrap 5 mm x 33 mm stent retrieval device placed across the occlusion.
Check angiogram revealed persistent occlusion of distal right M1 MCA.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by proglide closure device.
Total fluroscopic time: 42.6 min.
Total radiation dose : 1747 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Acute stroke - right distal MCA M1 segment occlusion - unsuccessful recanalisation with mechanical
thrombectomy.

BALLOON OCCLUSION TEST AND ENDOVACULAR COILING OF RIGHT INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY ANEURYSM AND PARENT ARTERY
OCCLUSION
Clinical profile: C/o right sided ptosis with a Wide necked large saccular aneurysm arising from the right
supraclinoid ICA.
Bilateral CFA access was taken and right CFA access secured with 6F infinity long sheath and left CFA access
secured with 4F short sheath. Through right CFA access, right carotid injection revealed a wide necked large
saccular aneurysm measuring 19.4x16 mm (FxH) with 6.3 mm wide neck arising from the paraophthalmic segment of
right ICA, with dome directed inferolaterally. An infundibulum measuring 3 mm in size was seen at the origin of
the ophthalmic artery.
Left intracranial internal carotid artery, bilateral anterior cerebral artery, middle cerebral artery and their
branches were normal. Parenchymal and venous phase images were normal.
Through right femoral access, 6 F envoy guiding catheter was placed in the right ICA. A Scepter XC 4 x 11mm
balloon was placed in the right petrous ICA and balloon occlusion test was performed. Patient had no
neurological deficit for the observation period of 20 min. Left carotid injection with balloon occlusion and
induced hypotension showed instantaneous filling of right ACA, with acceptable venous delay. Left vertebral
injection showed filling of right MCA and its branches and MCA through patent Pcom artery. Patient tolerated
the balloon occlusion well with no neurological deficits.
Under general anesthesia right ICA spin angiogram was done. A combination of Two Headway 17 microcatheter were
used to intubate the sac and neck of aneurysm. The sac of the aneurysm and the parent artery were occluded
using multiple detachable neuro coils of total length 345cm in distal to proximal direction. Further 125cm 4F
multipurpose catheter was placed in the petrous ICA and the internal carotid artery proximal to the aneurysm
was occluded using 8mmx14cm and 6mmx14cm Nester detachable coils (0.035").
Post embolization of the right internal carotid artery angiogram revealed complete occlusion of the aneurysm
with occlusion of the right internal carotid artery. Post procedure left carotid and angiograms revealed good
cross flow to the left side across the anterior communicating artery.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by proglide closure device on right side and manual compression on left
side.
Total fluroscopic time: 53mins.
Total radiation dose: 1985mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Wide necked large saccular aneurysm arising from the right para-opthalmic ICA - treated successfully with
endovascular aneurysm coiling and parent artery occlusion.

Clinical features: Central vein stenting was done in January 2022, discontinuation of anticoagulants.
Recurrence of right arm swelling.

level using a 18G intravenous cannula. Right common femoral vein were accessed and secured with 9F long sheath
and placed in SVC. Venogram was done from right cephalic vein access which showed a metallic stent in the right
brachiocephalic vein with a short segment high grade in stent stenosis with brisk flow in to multiple
collaterals. Using combination of Bernstein catheter and straight terumo wire the stenosis was crossed from the
femoral access and the distal accessed was secured with extra stiff wire in the right brachial vein. The
stenosis was dilated with mustang 8x40mm and cooks 10x40mm plain balloons until the waist disappears.
Post-dilatation venogram showed no significant residual stenosis and good forward flow in the right
brachiocephalic stent with disappearance of collaterals.
15min post dilatation venogram showed no residual stenosis / significant recoil.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total fluoroscopic time: 10.1mins.
Total Radiation dose: 103 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Case of right brachiocephalic vein in stent short segment stenosis was successfully treated with plain balloon
venoplasty.

PHARMACOMECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY & LEFT COMMON & EXTERNAL ILIAC VEIN STENTING
Clinical profile: Left lower limb DVT extending till IVC.
Under strict aseptic precautions and local anesthesia using USG guidance left popliteal vein was accessed and
secured with 9F sheath. Venogram of the left lower limb revealed thrombosis of popliteal vein, superficial
femoral vein, common femoral vein, left external and common iliac vein.
Over an extrastiff wire, 8F (105 cm) Angiojet, Zelante DVT catheter was advanced. Pulse spray thrombolysis was
initiated using 15 mg of Alteplase reconstituted in 100 ml of NS from iliac vein to femoral vein along the
length of the clot. Zelante catheter was exchanged for 50 cm perfusion catheter and Alteplase infusion was
started at 1 mg/h through the catheter with heparin infusion 500 U/h through the sheath. Venogram performed
after 4 hours significant burden of clots in ilio-femoral veins. Angiojet Rheolytic thrombectomy was done for
400 seconds using Angiojet Zelante catheter. Post-procedure venogram showed only mild residual thrombus in
superficial femoral and common femoral veins with flow limiting stenosis in left common and external iliac
iliac vein. Plain balloon angioplasty was done with 1x80 mm and 12x60 mm balloons. Post angioplasty angiogram
showed residual stenosis in the left common and external iliac with slow forward flow.
IVUS was done which showed significant narrowing of the left common iliac compressed by right iliac artery
crossing over left iliac vein suggesting may thurners syndrome and ilio-caval confluence was marked by IVUS and
simultaneous venogram from bilateral popliteal accesses.
E-luminex 14x10mm self-expanding metallic stent was deployed across the stenosis and post dilated with 12mm
plain balloon.
Check venogram showed no significant residual stenosis with forward flow across the stent.
Right popliteal sheath was removed and hemostasis achieved by manual compression.
Sheath left insitu in left popliteal vein and 1000 U/hr heparin through sheath.
Check angiogram performed the next day showed recurrent thrombus formation within the stent and in the left
external iliac vein with poor forward flow. 30 cm perfusion catheter was placed across the site of thrombus and
thrombolysis was Alteplase injection was run through it at 1 mg/h. Check angiogram performed after 7 hours of
catheter directed thrombolysis showed near complete recanalisation with partial non-occlusive thrombus within
the stent. In-stent angioplasty was done for the sticking thrombus using 12x60 mm Mustang balloon. Check
angiogram showed near complete recanalisation with good forward flow across the stent.
Sheath left insitu in left popliteal vein and 1000 U/hr heparin through sheath.
Sheath was removed the following day after confirming the stent patency on USG and hemostasis was achieved by
manual compression.
Total fluoroscopic time: 47.5 min.
Total Radiation dose: 891 mGy.
IMPRESSION:
Case of left lower limb extensive DVT with May thurners syndrome -treated with pharmacomechanical thrombectomy,
venoplasty and stenting of left common and external iliac vein.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH. P.

MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY FOR RIGHT MCA ACUTE STROKE
Clinical profile: Known HTN with acute CVA.
With all aseptic precautions, under local anesthesia and sedation, right CFA was accessed and secured with a 8F
short sheath. Using 4F Bernstein's catheter angiogram of right common carotid artery was performed which
demonstrated occlusion of the mid M1 segment of right MCA. Right ECA and its branches, ICA and ACA were normal
Infiniry plus 90cm guide sheath was navigated into proximal petrous ICA. A Triaxial system of vecta 74,
trevotrac 21 microcatheter and Traxcess Ex guidewire was used to cross the occlusion. vecta 74 was placed in
proximal M1 MCA. The stent retrieval device Solitaire X 6 x 40 mm was deployed across the occlusion.
First attempt of Mechanical thrombectomy was done using modified solumbra technique and angiogram revealed
TICI3 recanalization and ICAD related residual moderate stenosis of right M1 MCA.
Intra-arterial Tirofiban 10ml bolus was given through the vecta suction catheter and IV infusion of 7ml/hr was
started. 5 minutes check angio showed mild recoil with reduced flow in the MCA branches. Hence a 2mm x 12mm
coronary balloon angioplasty was planned. However, while navigating the balloon over a Traxcess wire, there
occurred a small non flow limiting dissection in the tortuous tonsillar loop of ICA. Hence, balloon
angioplasty was deferred. 20 minutes Angiogram following Tirofiban bolus showed stable stenosis of right M1
MCA with improved flow in MCA branches.
Post procedure angiogram showed TICI 3 recanalization with stable moderate right MCA stenosis and nonflow
limiting cervical ICA dissection.
Puncture site hemostasis was achieved by proglide closure device.
Total fluroscopic time: 25.8 min.
Total radiation dose : 1460 mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Acute stroke - right MCA M1 segment occlusion - treated successfully by mechanical thrombectomy with TICI 3
flow in right MCA territory with ICAD related moderate stenosis in right MCA.

Bilateral middle meningeal artery embosphere embolisation
Clinical details: Right sided chronic SDH, post evacuation.
Under local anaesthesia, strict aseptic precautions using modified seldinger technique, right common femoral
artery was punctured, secured with 5F 70 cm long sheath. Using 4F Berenstein catheter, bilateral CCA & ECA
angiograms were taken.
After priming ECA with 0.5 mg nimodipine, bilateral middle meningeal arteries were superselectively
catheterized with Merit Maestro microcatheter. Bilateral MMA were embolised with 100-300 micron embosphere
particles until stasis without any reflux.
Post procedure angiogram showed stasis of blood flow in bilateral MMA.
Sheath was removed and hemostasis achieved by manual compression
Total fluoroscopic time: 46.3 min
Total Radiation dose: 837.7 mGy
IMPRESSION:
Case of right sided chronic SDH - treated with bilateral middle meningeal artery embolization using
embospheres.

Follow up case of DVT- IVC filter successfully retrieved by transjugular approach.

LEFT PERONEAL AND POSTERIOR TIBIAL PLAIN BALLOON AND DEB ANGIOPLASTY
C/o: Restenosis of left PTA with Critical limb ischemia.
Under strict aseptic precautions under local anesthesia using modified Seldinger technique, left CFA was
accessed with 5F 45 cm sheath and angiogram of left lower limb taken. There was multifocal high grade
steno-occlusion of ATA from the origin with faint distal reformation, proximal peroneal artery high grade
stenosis, multifocal high grade stenosis of PTA. The left PTA steno-occlusions was crossed using a combination
of MPA catheter, merit maestro micro-catheter and Asahi Gladius 0.014 microwire. Angioplasty was performed
using Coyote2.0 x150mm plain balloon. Check angiogram showed embolic occlusion of distal PTA for which suction
thrombectomy was done two times using 4F multipurpose catheter. Patient was loaded with 13ml IV bolus of
tirofuse followed by 11ml/hr infusion. Check angiogram showed residual stenosis in distal PTA for which POBA
was done using Coyote2.5 x150mm plain balloon following which DEB angioplasty was done using 2.5x150, 2.5x100mm
balloons. Check angiogram showed good flow in PTA with occlusion of peroneal artery. Suction thrombectomy of
peroneal artery was done using 4F Berenstein followed by POBA with 2.5x150 balloon. Post procedure check
angiogram showed good flow across peroneal artery and PTA. Hemostasis at puncture site was obtained by Obtura
closure device..
Total fluoroscopic time: 39.7mins.
Total radiation dose : 235mGy.
CONCLUSION:
Case of proximal peroneal artery high grade stenosis, multifocal high grade stenosis of PTA -successfully
treated by plain balloon and DEB angioplasty.
Intraprocedure embolism to distal PTA - treated with suction thrombectomy.
DR.MATHEW CHERIAN / DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / DR.SANTHOSH P
