CLINICAL PROFILE: - Known case of traumatic spine and left tibial fractures post fixation 2 weeks back. Now
with non healing ulcer in the right heel.
RIGHT BELOW KNEE ANGIOPLASTY AND STENTING
Under strict aseptic precautions and using modified Seldinger's technique, left common femoral artery was
accessed secured with 4F short sheath. Angiograms of aortic bifurcation and right lower limb were obtained
using 4F Bernstein catheter.
Angiograms revealed normal aortic bifurcation, bilateral iliac, right common femoral and profunda femoral,
popliteal arteries. There was focal critical stenosis (99%) in osteo proximal ATA. Rest of the ATA was normal.
Peroneal and posterior tibial arteries were chronically occluded from its mid one third without any distal
reformation. ATA was supplying the angiosomes of foot.
4F short sheath was replaced with 5F 90cm sheath which was placed in distal right popliteal artery. Using a
Whisper coronary (0.014") wire the stenosis in proximal ATA was crossed and dilated with 2.5 mm x 80 mm plain
balloon. Since there was residual stenosis post angioplasty a coronary stent (2.5 mm x 12 mm Ultimaster,
Terumo) was deployed in the proximal ATA. Post procedure angiography showed stenosis good forward flow across
the ATA into angiosomes of foot without any residual stenosis or thrombosis. There was blush in the right heel
ulcer bed.
Sheath was removed and hemostasis was achieved by manual compression.
Total radiation dose: 82.2mGy
Total fluoroscopy time: 11.7mins
CONCLUSION:
" High grade stenosis in osteo proximal anterior tibial artery- treated with angioplasty and stenting.
" Chronic occlusion of peroneal artery and posterior tibial artery - not amenable to interventions.

DR.MATHEW CHERIAN/ DR.PANKAJ MEHTA / . P

visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
Intense tracer uptake noted involving the bilateral pulmonary nodules, largest measuring 1.5cm with an SUV max
of 8.5. Some of the nodules does not demonstrate increased tracer uptake.

intense tracer uptake and an SUV max of 12.6.
Minimal bilateral pleural effusion noted.
No other pathological focus of PSMA expression noted in the region of the chest.
No abnormalities are detected in breast, bilateral axilla or internal mammary node.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
Intense tracer uptake noted in soft tissue lesion involving the prostate gland, measuring 4.3x2.8cm with an SUV
max of 51.5. There is loss of fat plane with the posterior wall of bladder.
Intense tracer uptake noted involving the periportal, portocaval, paraaortic, aortocaval and retrocaval
lymphnodes, largest measuring 1.7cm with an SUV max of 21.
Intense tracer uptake noted involving hypodense lesions in both lobes of the liver, largest measuring
11.6x2.8cm with an SUV max of 70.8.
Multiple cortical cysts noted in both the kidneys, largest measuring 1.5cm with no significant tracer uptake.
No other pathological focus of PSMA expression noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Physiological tracer uptake noted in spleen, kidney, bladder and small bowel.
There is no hydroureteronephrosis .The gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the adrenals are unremarkable on this
study. There is no free fluid or loculated collection in the abdomen and pelvis.
SKELETAL:
Multiple sclerotic lesions noted involving vertebrae, bilateral ribs, right scapula, bilateral humeri,
bilateral ilium, right ischium, bilateral pubis and bilateral femori with intense tracer uptake an SUV max of
25.3.
IMPRESSION:
INTENSE TRACER UPTAKE NOTED IN SOFT TISSUE LESION INVOLVING THE PROSTATE GLAND; CONSISTENT WITH PRIMARY
MALIGNANCY.
INTENSE TRACER UPTAKE NOTED INVOLVING THE MEDIASTINAL, ABDOMINAL AND RETROPERITONEAL LYMPHNODES; CONSISTENT
WITH NODAL METASTASES.
INTENSE TRACER UPTAKE NOTED INVOLVING THE LUNG NODULES, LIVER AND SKELETAL LESIONS; CONSISTENT WITH WIDESPREAD
METASTASES.
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF INCREASED PSMA TRACER UPTAKE ELSEWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.

X-Ray - Breast.title: Clinical Indication: - Ca left breast, post-surgery, chemo and RT; for evaluation.
X-Ray - Breast.content:
Clinical Indication: - Ca left breast, post-surgery, chemo and RT; for evaluation.
Comparison is made to prior PET-CT dated 23-12-2019.
Technique:
Whole body images (base of skull to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq
of 18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 90mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the head and neck.
There is no significant cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the
cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and submandibular glands are unremarkable. The mastoid
air cells and the paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No focal mass lesion/mass effect is seen within the
visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
Mildly hypermetabolic uptake noted in the left breast skin thickening with an SUV max of 3.7.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the chest.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs, mediastinum and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Hypermtebaolic uptake noted in the terminal ileum and ileocaecal junction with an SUV max of 8.2 (?
Significance).
Liver parenchyma appears normal. Kidneys appear unremarkable. There is no hydroureteronephrosis .The
gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection
in the abdomen and pelvis. There is no significant retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy.
SKELETAL:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the extremities and musculo- skeletal system. There is no focal
suspicious lytic or blastic osseous lesion.
IMPRESSION:
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ANYWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.
MILDLY HYPERMETABOLIC UPTAKE NOTED IN THE LEFT BREAST SKIN THICKENING; NEEDS CLINICAL CORRELATION.
COMPARED TO PRIOR PET-CT DATED 23.12.2019, THERE IS NO RESIDUAL AND NO NEW LESIONS NOTED.
Dr K K Kamaleshwaran MD (Nuclear Medicine)
Consultant
Department of Nuclear Medicine & PET-CT

Technique:
Whole body images (base of skull to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq
of 18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 88mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the head and neck.
Intensely hypermetabolic uptake noted in both lobes of thyroid gland with an SUV max of 12. No nodules noted.
There is no significant cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the
cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and submandibular glands are unremarkable. The mastoid
air cells and the paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No focal mass lesion/mass effect is seen within the
visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
Intensely hypermetabolic enhancing necrotic soft tissue lesion noted in outer quadrant of the left breast,
measuring 1.8x1.6cm with an SUV max of 10.5.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the chest.
No abnormalities are detected in bilateral axilla or internal mammary node.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs, mediastinum and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Liver parenchyma appears normal. There is no hydroureteronephrosis .The gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the
adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection in the abdomen and pelvis. There is
no significant retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic adenopathy.
SKELETAL:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the extremities and musculo- skeletal system. There is no focal
suspicious lytic or blastic osseous lesion.
IMPRESSION:
INTENSELY HYPERMETABOLIC ENHANCING NECROTIC SOFT TISSUE LESION NOTED IN OUTER QUADRANT OF THE LEFT BREAST;
CONSISTENT WITH PRIMARY MALIGNANCY.
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ELSEWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.

X-Ray - Neck.title: 99m-TC SESTAMIBI PARATHYROID SCAN REPORT
X-Ray - Neck.content:
99m-TC SESTAMIBI PARATHYROID SCAN REPORT
Perfusion images and static images of anterior neck and chest were acquired at 20min and 1hr after IV inj of
99mTc-Sestamibi.
Findings:
Early static image at 20min shows tracer uptake in both the lobes of the thyroid and focus of uptake posterior
part of the right lobe of thyroid gland.
Delayed image at 1hr shows wash out of tracer from both lobes of thyroid gland with significant retention of
tracer in the posterior part of the right lobe of thyroid.
SPECT-CT demonstrates soft tissue lesion noted measuring 1.7x1.5cm in the posterior part of the right lobe of
the thyroid gland.
Impression:
SCAN FINDINGS SUGGESTIVE OF RIGHT INTRATHYROIDAL PARATHYROID ADENOMA / THYROID NODULE; NEEDS HPE CORRELATION.
NO EVIDENCE OF ANY OTHER FOCUS OF ABNORMAL TRACER CONCENTRATION IN THE REST OF THE HEAD, NECK AND CHEST
SUGGESTIVE OF ECTOPIC PARATHYROID ADENOMA.
Dr K K Kamaleshwaran MD (Nuclear Medicine)
Consultant
Department of Nuclear Medicine & PET-CT

X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.title: CT WHOLE BODY TRAUMA
X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.content:
CT WHOLE BODY TRAUMA
Serial sections of the brain followed by whole body extending from base of skull to the pelvis with
administration of I.V.contrast were studied.
C.T. SCAN OF BRAIN
Thin SAH seen in the right temporo-parietal sulci, sylvian fissure and along anterior interhemispheric fissure.
Few tiny hemorrhagic contusions noted in the gray white matter junction of right frontal lobe and in the right
side of genu of corpus callosum.
The C.P.Angles and posterior fossa contents are normal.
The ventricular system shows normal anatomical configuration.
There is no midline shift seen.
The basal cisterns, cortical sulci and sylvian fissures are normal.
The sella, parasellar and suprasellar regions are normal.
There is no evidence of fracture seen in the skull bones.
C.T.SCAN OF NECK
The nasopharynx and parapharngeal spaces appear normal.
There is no evidence of mass lesion seen in these regions.
The thyroid appears normal.
There is no evidence of mass around the thyroid.
Neck vessels appear normal.
Carotid and vertebral arteries appear normal.
Prevertebral soft tissues are normally seen.
Hyoid bone and laryngeal cartilages are normal.
C.T.SCAN OF THORAX
The study shows normal lung pattern with even distribution of the pulmonary arterial branches and that of the
bronchial tree.
The anatomical configuration of the structures in the mediastinum and both hilar regions are normal.
Horizontal fracture with irregular ramifications is noted involving the body of D5 and D6 extending to involve
the superior endplates. The fracture of D6 vertebrae involves both the anterior and posterior cortex. No
retropulsed fracture fragment or spinal canal compromise seen. No reduction in vertebral body height.
Significant pre and para vertebral soft tissue thickening noted at these levels - likely hematoma.
Consolidatory changes noted in the dependant segments of bilateral lungs with thin bilateral effusion.
Comminuted displaced fracture of body of left scapula seen.

X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.title: There is no evidence of hilar lymphadenopathy seen.
X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.content:
There is no evidence of hilar lymphadenopathy seen.
The arch of the aorta, aortic isthmus and descending thoracic aorta and the vessels arising from it are normal.
No traumatic aortic injury.
There is no evidence of pneumothorax.
Both domes of diaphragm are intact and normally placed.
No fracture ribs.
C.T. SCAN OF ABDOMEN
The study shows normal anatomical configuration of the liver. Diffuse fatty liver seen. No focal pathology is
noted.
The intrahepatic biliary radicles, portal and hepatic veins are normal.
The head, body and tail of the pancreas are well demonstrated and are normal in size, shape and attenuation.
The gall bladder is well distended and displays a normal wall.
No evidence of any stone, sludge or mass.
The spleen is normal with regard to size, position and morphology and displays uniform enhancement pattern.
Both the kidneys are normal in size, shape and position and show good excretion of contrast with adequate
demonstration of pelvicaliceal system.
The perinephric area is normal.
The adrenals are normal on both sides.
Aorta, IVC and paraaortic areas are normal. No retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy noted.
Medialization of the descending colon seen.
There is no free fluid seen in the abdomen / pneumoperitoneum.
The bladder is partially distended with foley in situ. No evidence of stone or mass.
Visualized bones are normal.
CT SCAN OF WHOLE SPINE
The spine is normal in alignment and curvature.
Craniovertebral junction ( Occipital condyles, C1, C2 ) - normal.
Thoracic vertebral fracture as described in thorax report. No evidence of any other fracture seen in rest of
the visualized vertebra.No evidence of any subluxation / dislocation of facetal joint.
All three vertebral columns are normal.No fracture / dislocation / subluxation seen.
IMPRESSION:
" Hemorrhagic contusions in the brain as mentioned - likely represent DAI.
" Right temporo-parietal and sylvian fissure SAH.
" Fractures of D5 and D6 vertebral body with pre/para vertebral hematoma as detailed. No retropulsed fracture
fragment or spinal canal compromise seen.
" Comminuted displaced fracture of body of left scapula.

X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.title: WHOLE BODY PET CT SCAN
X-Ray - Trauma & Whole Body.content:
WHOLE BODY PET CT SCAN
Clinical Indication: - Ca penis, post partial penectomy; for evaluation.
Technique:
Whole body images (base of skull to mid-thigh) were acquired in 3-D mode 60 min after IV Injection of 370 MBq
of 18F-FDG using a dedicated PET_CT scanner. Reconstruction of the acquired data was performed so as to obtain
fused PET CT images in transaxial, coronal, and sagittal views. Blood sugar level was checked before the scan
and was 115mg/dl.
Findings:
HEAD and NECK:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the head and neck.
There is no significant cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. The pharyngeal mucosal space, larynx and the
cervical trachea are unremarkable. The parotid glands and submandibular glands are unremarkable. The mastoid
air cells and the paranasal sinuses are unremarkable. No focal mass lesion/mass effect is seen within the
visualized brain parenchyma.
CHEST:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the chest.
No abnormalities are detected in breast, bilateral axilla or internal mammary node.
No abnormalities noted in the lungs, mediastinum and vasculature.
ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
Mildly hypermetabolic right external iliac and right inguinal lymphnodes are noted, largest measuring 2cm with
an SUV max of 4.
Ametabolic tiny left inguinal lymphnode noted, measuring 5mm.
No other pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the region of the abdomen and pelvis.
Liver parenchyma appears normal. Kidneys appear unremarkable. There is no hydroureteronephrosis. The
gallbladder, spleen; pancreas and the adrenals are unremarkable. There is no free fluid or loculated collection
in the abdomen and pelvis.
SKELETAL:
No pathological focus of FDG uptake noted in the extremities and musculo- skeletal system. There is no focal
suspicious lytic or blastic osseous lesion.
IMPRESSION:
NO DEFINITE EVIDENCE OF METABOLICALLY ACTIVE FDG AVID DISEASE ANYWHERE IN THE WHOLE BODY SURVEY.
MILDLY HYPERMETABOLIC RIGHT EXTERNAL ILIAC AND RIGHT INGUINAL LYMPHNODES; COULD BE REACTIVE ETIOLOGY. HOWEVER
NEEDS HPE / FOLLOWUP EVALUATION.
